The app calls this on launch and then about once a day. It answers two questions:

1. **Is there newer data?** Compare `dataPack.version` with the version the app already holds.
2. **Is this app still supported?** Send `appVersion`; if it is older than `minAppVersion` the answer is 426.

The response may be cached for a minute (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`).

get.description:
Every fact carries the source it came from and a `verification` flag. Pass `denomination` to get the facts about one note plus the facts about the currency as a whole.

**Checking for changes without downloading again.** The response has an `ETag` that changes whenever the facts do. Send it back in `If-None-Match`; if nothing changed the answer is `304 Not Modified` with no body. This is how the app keeps its saved copy current at almost no cost: show the saved facts at once, then make this conditional request in the background.

`Cache-Control: no-cache` means a cache may store the response but must revalidate it every time.

post.description:
Send the text the phone read from a note and get back the currency it belongs to.

**How it decides.** It looks for phrases printed on notes: the issuing bank (worth 0.5), the currency word (0.4), the country (0.3) and the ISO code (0.25). The distinct clues found are added up and capped at 1; each is listed in `evidence`. The answer is `matched` when the best candidate reaches 0.5 and leads the runner-up by at least 0.25.

**Always 200 for a valid request.** `unknown` and `ambiguous` are normal answers, not errors. Only a malformed request fails.

**Privacy.** The body is text only, at most 32 KB. Nothing is stored.

post.description:
Answers a question using only the facts in the catalogue, and streams the answer word by word as **server-sent events**, so the app can show it as it is written.

### The stream
The response is `text/event-stream`. Each message is `event: <name>` then `data: <json>`, ended by a blank line. Events arrive in this order:

| Event | Data | When |
|---|---|---|
| `sources` | `{ sources: [{ n, id, text, sourceName, sourceUrl }] }` | First, once. The facts the answer is built from; `[n]` in the answer refers to `n`. Empty when nothing matched. |
| `token` | `{ text }` | Many times. Append `text` to the answer. |
| `done` | `{ finishReason, answered }` | Last, once. `answered` is false when the facts did not cover the question. |
| `error` | the standard error body | Instead of `done`, if something fails after the stream has started. |

### Errors
- **Before the stream starts** (bad request, unknown currency, rate limit) you get an ordinary JSON error with the matching HTTP status.
- **After it starts** the status is already 200, so a failure arrives as an `error` event and the stream ends.
- **Closing the connection** cancels the answer immediately.

### What answers it
No language model is connected yet. The answer is made by quoting the best matching facts with their `[n]` numbers, so it can never say anything that is not in the catalogue. If no fact matches, the answer is "I don't have that information yet." and `answered` is false. A model will replace this without changing the stream.

**Rate limit:** 10 requests per minute per address, on top of the general limit.

info.title: Currency Reader API
info.description:
The HTTP API behind the **Currency Reader** app. The phone reads a banknote with its camera and OCR, then uses this API to find out which currency it is, fetch sourced facts about it, and answer questions.

## Try it
Use **Try it out** on any endpoint below. For a first look:

1. `GET /v1/currencies`: see what the catalogue holds.
2. `POST /v1/scan/resolve` with the example body: it names a currency from OCR text.
3. `GET /v1/currencies/EUR/facts`: read the facts; copy the `ETag` and send it back as `If-None-Match` to see `304`.
4. `POST /v1/ask`: stream an answer. (The docs page can show only the final text; `curl -N` shows it arriving.)

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/v1/scan/resolve -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"lines":["EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK","EURO","20"]}'

curl -N localhost:3000/v1/ask -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"What colour is the 20 euro note?","isoCode":"EUR"}'
```

## What is real today
| Part | State |
|---|---|
| Endpoints, validation, errors, rate limits | Working and tested. |
| Catalogue | A small hand-written starter set (4 currencies). Every fact is marked `unverified`. Held in memory; a database replaces it later. |
| Answers (`/v1/ask`) | Quote the best matching facts. **No language model is connected yet.** |
| Looking up currencies that are not in the catalogue | Not built. `/v1/scan/resolve` answers `unknown`. |
| Exchange rates | Not built. |
| Feedback storage | In memory only; lost on restart. |

## Conventions

**Versioning.** Endpoints live under `/v1`. A breaking change gets `/v2`; `/v1` keeps working. Health checks are not versioned.

**Content type.** Requests with a body must send `Content-Type: application/json`. Bodies are limited to 32 KB. The API never accepts images.

**Unknown fields are rejected.** A misspelled field returns `VALIDATION_FAILED` instead of being ignored, so mistakes show up while developing.

**Request ID.** Every response has an `x-request-id` header, and every error body repeats it as `requestId`. You may send your own `x-request-id` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters); otherwise one is generated. Quote it when reporting a problem.

**Rate limits.** 60 requests per minute per client address, and 10 per minute on `/v1/ask`. Over the limit, the answer is `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. The health checks are exempt.

**Caching.** Facts carry an `ETag`. Send it back in `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` when nothing has changed.

## Errors
Every failure, from any endpoint, has the same JSON body:

```json
{
  "status": 404,
  "code": "CURRENCY_NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "No currency with the code 'XYZ'.",
  "hint": "List the supported codes with GET /v1/currencies.",
  "retryable": false,
  "requestId": "8f14e45f-ceea-467a-9575-1c9d0b1f0a11",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-08T10:15:30.000Z",
  "path": "/v1/currencies/XYZ"
}
```

- **Branch on `code`**, never on `message`: the code is stable, the wording may change.
- `retryable` says whether the same request may succeed later. If false, change the request.
- `details` appears for `VALIDATION_FAILED` and lists each bad field.
- Server faults (`INTERNAL_ERROR`) never include internal detail; use `requestId` to find them in the log.

| Code | HTTP | Retry? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 400 | no | One or more fields are missing, the wrong type, or out of range. `details` lists each one. |
| `INVALID_JSON` | 400 | no | The request body is empty or is not valid JSON. |
| `BAD_REQUEST` | 400 | no | The request was rejected for a reason that has no more specific code. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | no | The Content-Type is not application/json. |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no | The request body is larger than 32 KB. |
| `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no | There is no endpoint at that path or method. |
| `CURRENCY_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no | No currency with that ISO 4217 code is in the catalogue. |
| `DENOMINATION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no | The currency exists but has no such denomination. |
| `APP_UPDATE_REQUIRED` | 426 | no | The app is older than the minimum version this server supports. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes | Too many requests from this address. See the Retry-After header. |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | yes | The server is running but a part it needs is not ready. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | yes | Something went wrong on the server. It is not caused by your request. |
